flagged_unverifiable: All 17 image-based problems (choropleth-uk.png, isotherm-uk.png, isobar-uk.png, isohyet-uk.png) were left with their stored solutions untouched: the maps cannot be read by this agent. Every stored answer is internally consistent (multiple-choice indices in range, temperatures and pressures inside the isoline values named in the display, no negative distances), so nothing was changed.

bronze[3] (Point A between isobars, stored answer 1012 mb and 1016 mb): the walk asks the student to read the lower then the higher of the two lines either side of A. The lower/higher labelling is taken from the stored answer, not from the map. If the map places A elsewhere, both the answer and the walk would need the same correction.

bronze[4] / gold[0] (isohyet P and Q): the walk uses P between the 800 and 1000 mm lines and Q between the 600 and 800 mm lines, which is exactly what the original misconception text asserted and is the only reading consistent with the stored difference. Not independently verified against the image.

silver[5] (P minus Q temperature difference, stored answer 2): the walk uses P between the 6°C and 8°C isotherms and Q between the 4°C and 6°C isotherms, again taken from the original misconception text rather than from the image.

bronze[2] (P just south of the 8°C isotherm): the walk deduces a 2°C isotherm interval from the 4, 6 and 8 labels used elsewhere in this lesson, and frames the next line south as conditional ('if the 2°C steps continue') so no unverified map fact is asserted.
opener_concept: Four map areas shaded pale to dark (inline SVG) with a four-band key underneath. Box 1 asks which area is darkest, which any student answers by eye. Box 2 reads the darkest band's lower limit off the key, box 3 reads the palest band's upper limit, which quietly exposes the fact that a shade only pins you to a range. The reveal names what they just did as reading a choropleth, and points forward to isolines.
